scheme_name: PM Van Mitra Scheme – Urban Forestry
overview: The PM Van Mitra Scheme – Urban Forestry is a government initiative under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change aimed at promoting urban forestry and green cover in cities. It focuses on increasing tree plantation in urban areas to combat pollution, enhance biodiversity, and improve the quality of life for urban residents. The scheme encourages community participation, including citizens, NGOs, and local bodies, in developing and maintaining urban forests. It aligns with national goals of environmental sustainability and climate resilience.
objectives: Increase urban green cover through tree plantation in cities
Combat air pollution and improve urban environmental quality
Promote community participation in urban forestry initiatives
Develop and maintain urban forests as carbon sinks
Support climate resilience and adaptation in urban areas
Create awareness about the importance of trees in cities
Integrate urban forestry into city planning and development
eligibility: The scheme is open to citizens, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), resident welfare associations, municipal corporations, urban local bodies, and other community groups interested in undertaking urban forestry projects. Applicants must propose viable tree plantation and maintenance plans in urban areas, with preference given to projects involving native species and community engagement.
benefits: Financial assistance for tree plantation and maintenance, technical guidance on species selection and plantation techniques, recognition for outstanding contributions to urban greening, capacity building through training and workshops, and support for long-term sustainability of urban green spaces.
financial_support: The scheme provides financial support in the form of subsidies for tree plantation, including costs for saplings, planting materials, and maintenance for a specified period. The exact quantum and mechanism of support are determined based on project proposals and availability of funds under the scheme.
application_process: 1. Identify a suitable urban area for tree plantation. 2. Prepare a project proposal detailing the plantation plan, species selection, maintenance strategy, and community involvement. 3. Submit the proposal to the designated nodal officer or through the official portal of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. 4. Await review and approval by the concerned authorities. 5. Upon approval, receive financial and technical support to implement the project. 6. Execute the plantation and maintenance activities as per the approved plan. 7. Submit periodic progress reports and utilization certificates.
required_documents: Land ownership or usage permission documents
Details of proposed tree species and quantities
Information about the implementing agency or group
Commitment letter for community participation (if applicable)
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Applications are accepted throughout the year subject to fund availability.
implementing_agency: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
caveats: Funding is subject to availability of budget under the scheme
Projects must ensure survival and maintenance of planted saplings for a minimum period
Preference is given to projects using native and ecologically suitable species
Beneficiaries are responsible for long-term maintenance after initial support period
Duplicate funding for the same activity from other government schemes may not be permitted
